Earlier this year, Apple closed off parts of the Apple Park Visitor Center, saying at the time that it was for "improvements to our store."

The space has now reopened, and the biggest change is that Apple has removed the experience that used to let visitors explore Apple Park through augmented reality (AR) using specially configured iPads.

The Apple Park Visitor Center opened to the public in 2017, and here's how the company described the AR experience at the time:

Using augmented reality to bring a model of the campus to life, visitors can explore Apple Park in an immersive and interactive way. Visitors can learn about the world's largest naturally ventilated building space and get a glimpse at one of the world's largest on-site solar installations. Visitors can also choose to lift the entire roof to reveal the collaborative workspace layout inside the building.

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was divided into three areas: an AR exhibit, a traditional Apple Store, and a café.

Apple has now removed the AR exhibit and converted the space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. According to MacRumors, the changes include wall-lined Avenues accessory displays and redesigned tables showcasing Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the café, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac's Take

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was certainly unique, but after nine years, the space was starting to feel like it could be put to better use.

I was hoping Apple would try something else instead of turning it into just another generic retail store, but thankfully the café remains as one of the distinctive elements of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
